04 / Independent product prototype

FlowList

A playlist-ordering tool that turns a collection of tracks into a proposed listening sequence. It uses metadata and estimated features, not audio analysis.

OverviewEngineeringResults & evidence
Role
Independent project
When
2026 / ongoing
Stack
Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind
Status
Metadata-based prototype

What I built

  • A flow-selection and sequencing pipeline with chapter structure, transition costs and deterministic output.
  • Editable results: reorder tracks, lock endpoints, compare with the original order and recompute transitions.
  • Platform import/export code and optional feedback collection, with real-account validation kept separate from local checks.
Open public demo ↗See captured result ↗

Order is the product

The tool proposes an order for tracks already in a playlist. Users select a playlist type and a flow, such as an energy wave or a progression from scattered material toward coherence. The result includes chapter positions and explanations for transitions.

The estimates come from metadata and deterministic heuristics. A mood label or approximate BPM range is not a measurement of the recording.

Structure first, transitions second

Local refinement uses a bounded search rather than testing every permutation. Chapter-sensitive strategies refine within chapters, soft landings remain protected, and loop strategies include the last-to-first transition. Repeated occurrences are preserved by their position in the input, not collapsed by track ID.

Give the listener control

The newer result-editor code adds confidence labels, endpoint locks, manual reordering and comparison with the original playlist. After an edit, transitions are recomputed instead of leaving explanations attached to an obsolete order.

These controls let users revise a heuristic proposal. Their presence in the local code does not establish that every control is available in the older public deployment shown below.

Export is a separate boundary

YouTube export code includes OAuth, review before creation and resuming an interrupted export. Apple Music paths retain provider track IDs across import and export. Cross-platform track matching is not implemented.

A text export and a provider write are different operations. Real Google and Apple account writes still need an owner-account smoke test; I do not describe those integrations as production-validated.

A real demo result

What the checks establish

The sequencing checks exercise 54 strategy cards and 135 dual-card combinations for structural properties. This checks constraints and consistent output, not whether listeners prefer the resulting order.

The public demo was run through to a result for this case study. Newer local editor, provider-export and feedback code has implementation checks, but real-account export and real-user feedback remain unverified.

What I still need to learn

The next useful evidence is a listener comparing an original order with the proposed sequence, making edits and explaining the transitions that do not work. Metadata estimates alone cannot validate musical continuity. No improved listening-quality score is claimed here.
